definition: The two user-facing latency metrics: how long until output starts (dominated by prefill and queueing) and how fast it streams (dominated by decode).
details: The two user-facing latency metrics: how long until output starts (dominated by prefill and queueing) and how fast it streams (dominated by decode). Interactive products live and die by TTFT; batch pipelines care about total throughput.

explainer.lead: Tokens per second covers the two user-facing latency metrics: time until output starts and how fast it streams. It matters because interactive products live and die by time to first token, while batch pipelines care about total throughput.

tiers.eli5: One number is how long you wait before the answer begins, the other is how fast it types. Waiting is worse than slow typing for chat; the reverse can be true for bulk jobs.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers tune prefill, queueing and decode separately to hit targets for each metric. A common pitfall is optimizing streaming speed while ignoring time to first token in an interactive product.
tiers.paperLevel: Time to first token is dominated by prefill and queueing; streaming rate is dominated by decode. Throughput and latency trade off against each other.

explainer.example: A chat app failing on time to first token feels broken even if it streams fast; a nightly batch job cares mainly about total throughput.
